crime-high.input: I want a route with very high crime rate.

crime-low.input: Avoid high crime density and prefer lower historical reported crime density.

architecture.input: I want more historic architecture along my walking route.

nature.input: I want more trees and greener streets.

food.input: I want bagels and cappuccino along the route.

multi.input: I want architecture, more trees, and a coffee shop along the route.

waterfront-high.input: I want a waterfront walk along the river.

personalized_score.formula: Weighted core experience and independent complaint-density fit − detour penalty − weather adjustment

crime.normalization: density / (density + fixed graph p95 neighbourhood density); reverse for low. No hard clipping.

crime.area_method: length × 2 × corridor width; not a polygon-union area. Primary measure is unique complaints per route kilometre.
crime.coordinate_accuracy: NYPD published approximate/block-level coordinates; not independently surveyed
limitations: Reported complaints, not victimization rates or personal risk. No population/activity denominator.
Occurrence dates and approximate published block-level coordinates; not live street conditions.
Most serious recorded offense only; reporting and policing patterns affect counts.
Snapshot is source-bounded and delayed; later reports and corrections can change historical counts.
Bounding-box plausibility does not independently verify every coordinate or borough.
Unknown boroughs remain unknown; no demographic fields are retained.
